name: WeKnora
description: Open-source LLM knowledge platform: turn raw documents into a queryable RAG, an autonomous reasoning agent, and a self-maintaining Wiki.
one_liner: Turns a pile of a company's own documents into a searchable, chatty knowledge base: ask it a question in plain language and it answers using only your files, not the open internet.
buyer: An operations manager at a firm with lots of internal documentation (policies, contracts, manuals) that staff constantly dig through manually.
business_use_cases: A law firm builds a private, self-hosted Q&A system over its case files and precedent documents so associates get answers in seconds instead of searching folders.
A manufacturer turns its equipment manuals and SOPs into a chat interface for the shop floor.
An IT consultancy offers 'internal knowledge base setup' as a fixed-price package for clients drowning in scattered documentation.

money_ideas.idea: Offer fixed-price 'private knowledge base' implementation for firms with sensitive documents that can't use cloud AI
Charge a monthly fee for hosting, updates, and support of the deployed system

steal_this: This weekend, deploy it against one local business's public documents (manuals, policies) as a live demo, then pitch the paid private version.
